questions.question: Sa pangungusap na “Malamig ang simoy ng hangin,” ano ang pinakamalapit na kahulugan ng “simoy”?
questions.note: Ang simoy ay banayad na galaw o daloy ng hangin.

questions.question: Alin ang wastong gamit ng “nang” sa pangungusap?
questions.note: Ginagamit ang nang sa pang-abay na paraan o panahon, gaya ng “nang maaga.”

questions.question: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng sawikaing “makapal ang mukha”?

choices.B: Walang hiya o hindi madaling mapahiya

questions.note: Tumutukoy ito sa kawalan ng hiya o pagiging hindi alintana ang puna.

questions.question: Which part of the body is the 'siko'?
questions.note: Tuhod = knee, balikat = shoulder, pulso = wrist.

questions.question: What does 'masarap' mean?
questions.note: Maanghang = spicy, mahal = expensive, sobrang luto = overcooked.

questions.question: Who is called 'Kuya' in a Filipino family?
questions.note: Kuya is the respectful term for an older brother or older male.

questions.question: What is 'apatnapu' in English?
questions.note: Labing-apat = 14, apat na raan = 400, animnapu = 60.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word means 'cloud'?
questions.note: Ulan = rain, hangin = wind, kidlat = lightning.

questions.question: Which word is the opposite of 'mabigat'?
questions.note: Mabigat = heavy; magaan = light. Makapal = thick, malambot = soft, matibay = sturdy.

questions.question: Who is your 'pamangkin'?
questions.note: Pinsan = cousin, apo = grandchild, inaanak = godchild.

questions.question: Alin ang pangungusap na gumagamit ng “kung” bilang pangatnig na nagsasaad ng kondisyon?

choices.A: Hindi ko alam kung saan siya nakatira.
choices.D: Sabihin mo kung sino ang nanalo.

questions.note: Ang “kung magsasanay ka” ay nagtatakda ng kondisyong kailangang matupad.

questions.question: Sa “Sinulatan ni Lito ng liham si Mara,” sino ang tumatanggap ng liham?
questions.note: Si Mara ang tumatanggap ng liham; si Lito ang tagaganap at ang liham ang isinulat.

questions.question: Ano ang kaibahan ng “kailangan kong umalis” at “kailangan ko nang umalis”?

choices.B: Ang una ay nagsasaad ng pangangailangan; ang ikalawa ay nagsasaad na oras na o dapat nang gawin ito
choices.C: Ang una ay nakaraan; ang ikalawa ay hinaharap
choices.D: Ang una ay pakiusap; ang ikalawa ay utos

questions.note: Ang “nang” ay nagbibigay-diin sa pagkaapurahan o pagiging napapanahon ng pag-alis.

questions.question: Which part of the face is the 'kilay'?
questions.note: Pilikmata = eyelash, noo = forehead, talukap = eyelid.

questions.question: Which word describes a light drizzle?
questions.note: Hamog = dew, baha = flood, ulap = cloud.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word means 'earthquake'?
questions.note: Bagyo = typhoon, baha = flood, pagguho = collapse/landslide.

questions.question: What feeling does 'Sayang!' express?
questions.note: 'Sayang' laments something wasted or a missed chance.

questions.question: What number is 'isang libo't limang daan'?
questions.note: Isang libo (1,000) + limang daan (500) = 1,500.

questions.question: Which verb means 'to borrow' an item?
questions.note: Magpahiram = to lend, magsauli = to return, magbenta = to sell.

questions.question: What attitude does 'Bahala na' most commonly express?
questions.note: 'Bahala na' means come what may, leaving the result to fate or God.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamalinaw na halimbawa ng pangungusap na may di-tuwirang pahayag?

choices.B: Sinabi ni Ana na uuwi siya.

questions.note: Iniuulat ng di-tuwirang pahayag ang sinabi nang walang tuwirang sipi at karaniwang nagbabago ang panghalip.

questions.question: Sa “Nagluto si Ben ng adobo para sa kaniyang lola,” anong papel ang ginagampanan ng “para sa kaniyang lola”?
questions.note: Ang lola ang nakikinabang sa pagluluto.

questions.question: Aling pares ang pinakamalinaw na nagpapakita ng pagkakaiba ng aspektong naganap at nagaganap?
questions.note: Ang “kumain” ay naganap; ang “kumakain” ay nagaganap o nagpapatuloy.

questions.question: In 'Ang matandang lalaki ay umalis kahapon,' which word is the pang-uri?
questions.note: Matanda (old) describes lalaki. Umalis = verb, kahapon = adverb of time.

questions.question: Someone who is 'mababaw ang luha'…
questions.note: Literally 'shallow tears': tears come easily.

questions.question: Following the standard rin/din rule, which sentence is correct?
questions.note: Use 'rin' after vowels (masaya) and 'din' after consonants (mabait, malungkot).

questions.question: In Filipino tradition, who is the 'ilaw ng tahanan'?
questions.note: The father is the 'haligi ng tahanan' (pillar); the mother is the light.

questions.question: 'Ang hindi lumingon sa pinanggalingan ay hindi makararating sa paroroonan' teaches…
questions.note: Those who forget their origins will not reach their destination.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word refers to dusk?
questions.note: Bukang-liwayway = dawn, tanghaling-tapat = high noon, hatinggabi = midnight.

questions.question: Which word refers to a place near the listener but away from the speaker?
questions.note: Dito = near the speaker, doon = far from both, saan = where.

questions.question: Sa “Ipinanghiwa ni Rosa ng mangga ang matalim na kutsilyo,” ano ang pokus ng pandiwa?
questions.note: Ang kutsilyo ang gamit na ipinanghiwa.

questions.question: Alin ang may pinakamalinaw na wastong gamit ng “may” at “mayroon”?
questions.note: Maaaring gamitin ang “mayroon” bago ang panghalip at pangngalan sa ganitong ayos.

questions.question: Ano ang pangunahing pagkakaiba ng “Hindi siya umalis dahil umulan” at “Hindi siya umalis, kaya umulan”?

choices.B: Sa una, ang ulan ang dahilan ng hindi pag-alis; sa ikalawa, ipinapahiwatig na ang hindi pag-alis ang sanhi ng ulan
choices.C: Sa una ay kondisyon; sa ikalawa ay paghahambing

questions.note: Nagbabago ang ugnayang sanhi-bunga dahil sa ayos ng “dahil” at “kaya.”

questions.question: Sa “Binasa ng mga mag-aaral ang sanaysay,” bakit “ang sanaysay” ang paksa sa karaniwang pagsusuring Filipino?

choices.A: Dahil ito ang gumagawa ng kilos
choices.B: Dahil ito ang layong binibigyang-pansin ng pandiwa
choices.C: Dahil ito ang nagsasaad ng lugar

questions.note: Ang pokus sa layon ay nagtatampok sa sanaysay; hindi sapat ang pagiging una o huli sa pangungusap.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamainam na rebisyon upang maiwasan ang kalabuan sa “Nakita niya ang lalaki gamit ang teleskopyo”?

choices.A: Nakita niya ang lalaki, at may teleskopyo.
choices.B: Gamit ang teleskopyo, nakita niya ang lalaki.
choices.C: Nakita niya ang lalaki gamit niya.
choices.D: Ang lalaki ay nakita niya gamit.

questions.note: Inilalapit ng ayos ang pariralang “gamit ang teleskopyo” sa kilos na inilalarawan.

questions.question: Which verb form means the action was just completed?
questions.note: Katatapos aspect: kakakain = just ate.

questions.question: Someone who is 'kapit sa patalim' is…
questions.note: Literally gripping a blade: doing something risky out of desperation.

questions.question: Which word is closest in meaning to 'marilag'?
questions.note: Marilag = beautiful/majestic. Marahas = violent, malagim = gruesome, matayog = lofty.

questions.question: A person described as 'taingang-kawali'…
questions.note: Literally 'frying-pan ears': deliberately ignoring what is said.

questions.question: Which marker correctly completes: '___ Maria at Jose ay magkapatid'?
questions.note: 'Sina' is the plural form of 'si' for two or more named people.

questions.question: Sa “Ipinagpagawa ni Mila ng bahay ang kaniyang mga magulang,” sino ang benepisyaryo ng kilos?
questions.note: Ang mga magulang ang pinaglaanan ng pagpapagawa ng bahay.

questions.question: Aling pares ang wastong nagtatangi sa pokus sa ganapan at pokus sa layon?

choices.A: Pinagtaniman ni Nena ng gulay ang bakuran / Itinanim ni Nena ang gulay
choices.B: Nagtanim si Nena / Nagtatanim si Nena
choices.C: Kumain si Nena / Kinain ni Nena
choices.D: Magluluto si Nena / Nagluluto si Nena

questions.note: Sa una, bakuran ang ganapan; sa ikalawa, gulay ang layong binibigyang-pansin.

questions.question: Bakit hindi laging mapagpapalit ang “daw” at “raw” sa pormal na pagsulat?

choices.A: Magkaiba ang kahulugan ng dalawa sa lahat ng pangungusap
choices.B: Nakabatay ang pagpili sa tunog na sinusundan, bagaman may baryasyon sa aktuwal na gamit
choices.C: Ang “daw” ay para lamang sa nakaraan

questions.note: Karaniwang tuntunin: “daw” pagkatapos ng katinig, “raw” pagkatapos ng patinig, maliban sa ilang tunog at baryasyon.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamahusay na paliwanag sa “Nakapag-aral siya nang mabuti” kumpara sa “Nakapag-aral siya ng mabuti”?

choices.B: Ang “nang mabuti” ay naglalarawan kung paano nag-aral; ang “ng mabuti” ay hindi angkop sa kahulugang iyon
choices.C: Ang “ng mabuti” ay nangangahulugang sa mabuting paaralan

questions.note: Ang “nang” ay ginagamit dito upang ilarawan ang paraan ng pag-aaral.

questions.question: Aling pangungusap ang may lohikal na problema sa pagtukoy sa gumagawa ng kilos?

choices.A: Nang matapos ang klase, umuwi ang mga mag-aaral.
choices.B: Pagdating sa bahay, sinalubong ni Carlo ang aso.

questions.note: Sa “Pagkatapos magluto,” tila ang ulam ang nagluto; kailangang tukuyin ang taong nagluto.

questions.question: An awit has 12 syllables per line. How many does a korido have?
questions.note: Korido (e.g., Ibong Adarna) uses 8-syllable lines; awit (Florante at Laura) uses 12.

questions.question: A person described as 'bukas-palad' is…
questions.note: Open-palmed: generous. Open-minded is 'bukas ang isip'.

questions.question: Which Tagalog word comes from Sanskrit?
questions.note: Guro comes from Sanskrit 'guru'; mesa, bintana, bapor come from Spanish.

questions.question: 'Isang kahig, isang tuka' describes someone who…
questions.note: One scratch, one peck: earning just enough for each meal.

questions.question: In baybayin, a kudlit placed above a character changes its vowel to…
questions.note: Above = e/i, below = o/u. The vowel-cancelling mark was a later Spanish addition.

questions.question: Sa “Ipinangtakip ni Lira sa palayok ang dahon ng saging,” anong papel ang itinatampok ng “dahon ng saging”?
questions.note: Ang dahon ang instrumentong ginamit na pantakip.

questions.question: Sa “Sinulatan ni Marco ng liham ang kaniyang kaibigan,” ano ang papel ng “ang kaniyang kaibigan”?

choices.C: Ang taong pinaglaanan o pinadalhan ng liham

questions.note: Ang kaibigan ang pinaglaanan ng liham; si Marco ang tagaganap at ang liham ang isinulat.

questions.question: Alin ang nagpapakita ng pagkakaiba ng “makapagsulat” at “makasulat” sa karaniwang gamit?

choices.A: Laging magkapareho ang anyo at kahulugan
choices.B: Ang una ay maaaring magdiin sa kakayahang magsulat; ang ikalawa ay maaaring magdiin sa pagkakaroon ng pagkakataong maisulat ang isang bagay
choices.C: Ang una ay pangngalan; ang ikalawa ay pang-uri
choices.D: Ang ikalawa ay laging nasa aspektong naganap

questions.note: Nagkakapatong ang gamit ng mga anyo, ngunit maaaring magkaiba ang diin sa kakayahan at pagkakagawa.

questions.question: Sa “Ikinagalit ni Rosa ang mapanuyang komento,” ano ang pokus ng pandiwa?
questions.note: Ang mapanuyang komento ang sanhi ng galit.

questions.question: Alin ang pinakamalinaw na dahilan kung bakit maaaring mag-iba ang pakahulugan ng “na” sa Tagalog?

choices.B: Maaari itong maging pang-angkop, pangatnig, o bahagi ng anyong pandiwa depende sa konteksto

questions.note: Maraming gamit ang “na”; kailangang suriin ang sintaks at konteksto.

questions.question: Which completes: 'Sina Ana, Ben, at Carlo ay ___'?
questions.note: Magkapatid = two siblings; three or more = magkakapatid.

questions.question: Which word contains a gitlapi (infix)?
questions.note: Sumayaw = s-um-ayaw. In 'umalis' the root starts with a vowel, so um- is an unlapi.

questions.question: Which sentence means 'The child was bitten by the dog'?
questions.note: Object focus: 'ng aso' is the biter, 'ang bata' was bitten. The others mean the child bit the dog.

questions.question: What is the salitang-ugat of 'nagsipagtakbuhan'?
questions.note: Nagsipag- + takbo + -han. 'Sipag' only looks like it is inside.

questions.question: Which pair are antonyms (magkasalungat)?
questions.note: Humble vs. arrogant. The other pairs are synonyms.

questions.question: Why did early river-valley states often develop near large rivers?

choices.B: Floodplains supplied water and fertile soil, supporting food surpluses
choices.C: Rivers eliminated the need for government
choices.D: River water made metal tools unnecessary

questions.note: Reliable water and fertile alluvium supported intensive agriculture and larger settlements.

questions.question: Which feature most clearly distinguishes a primary source from a later historical account?

choices.B: It was created during the period or by a participant/witness being studied

questions.note: Primary sources originate in the period or from participants, though they still require critical evaluation.

questions.question: Why did the Roman Republic develop checks such as separate magistracies and a Senate?

choices.A: To guarantee equal power for every resident
choices.B: To limit concentration of authority among competing elites and offices

questions.note: Republican institutions distributed authority, though political equality remained limited.

questions.question: Which ship sank in 1912 after striking an iceberg?
questions.note: The Lusitania was torpedoed in 1915; the Britannic hit a mine in 1916.

questions.question: Who co-wrote 'The Communist Manifesto' with Friedrich Engels?
questions.note: Published in 1848, decades before Lenin's revolution.

questions.question: Whose 1492 voyage reached the Americas for Spain?
questions.note: Da Gama sailed to India for Portugal; Magellan's voyage began in 1519.

questions.question: In which country did the Renaissance begin?
questions.note: It began in Italian city-states like Florence in the 14th century.

questions.question: Who led Nazi Germany during World War II?
questions.note: Mussolini led Fascist Italy; Bismarck and Wilhelm II were earlier German leaders.

questions.question: Which city was divided by a wall from 1961 to 1989?
questions.note: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
questions.note: Built in the Peruvian Andes in the 15th century.

questions.question: Why did the printing press help the Reformation spread?

choices.A: It made every European literate immediately
choices.B: It lowered the cost and increased the speed of reproducing arguments and pamphlets
choices.D: It prevented religious texts from being translated

questions.note: Printing multiplied the circulation of reformist texts without eliminating illiteracy or censorship.

questions.question: Which factor most weakened feudal relationships in parts of Western Europe after the Black Death?

choices.A: A sudden disappearance of all monarchies
choices.B: Labor scarcity that improved bargaining power for some surviving workers

questions.note: Population loss raised the relative value of labor, although effects varied by region.

questions.question: Why did the Mongol Empire sometimes facilitate long-distance trade across Eurasia?

choices.A: It removed every tax and conflict permanently
choices.B: Imperial control over extensive routes could improve protection and connectivity
choices.C: It prohibited merchants from crossing borders
choices.D: It moved all trade to sea routes

questions.note: Mongol rule connected broad territories and could secure routes, despite periods of violence and disruption.

questions.question: Which revolution began with the storming of the Bastille?
questions.note: July 14, 1789, Paris.

questions.question: Suleiman the Magnificent ruled which empire?
questions.note: He reigned 1520–1566.

questions.question: Who was Britain's Prime Minister for most of World War II?
questions.note: Churchill served 1940–1945; Chamberlain led at the war's start.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek city-state was famous for its military discipline?
questions.note: Spartan boys entered the agoge military training system.

questions.question: Which country modernized rapidly during the Meiji Restoration?
questions.note: Began in 1868.

questions.question: Who was the first emperor of a unified China?
questions.note: He unified China in 221 BC.

questions.question: Which document begins with 'We the People'?
questions.note: The Declaration begins 'When in the Course of human events'.

questions.question: Which comparison between the French and Haitian Revolutions is most accurate?

choices.B: Both invoked liberty and equality, but the Haitian Revolution directly overturned slavery and colonial racial hierarchy
choices.C: The Haitian Revolution preceded the French Revolution
choices.D: The French Revolution was led by enslaved plantation workers

questions.note: The Haitian Revolution transformed universalist revolutionary language into a struggle against slavery and colonial rule.

questions.question: Why did industrialization initially increase many cities' public-health problems?

choices.B: Urban growth often outpaced housing, sanitation, and clean-water infrastructure
choices.C: Industrial workers refused all public services
choices.D: Cities no longer needed food imports

questions.note: Rapid urbanization overwhelmed infrastructure in many industrial centers.

questions.question: Why was the Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) organized around a balance of power?

choices.B: To prevent any single state from dominating Europe after the Napoleonic Wars
choices.C: To create a unified democratic Europe
choices.D: To give France permanent control of the continent

questions.note: Diplomats sought a stable arrangement that constrained renewed hegemony.

questions.question: Which Roman leader crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC?
questions.note: The crossing started Caesar's civil war with Pompey.

questions.question: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
questions.note: Late 18th century, led by textiles, coal, and steam.

questions.question: Which statesman led the unification of Germany in 1871?
questions.note: Bismarck was Prussia's minister-president.

questions.question: The Silk Road mainly linked China with which region?
questions.note: Overland routes ran through Central Asia to the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Which civilization developed cuneiform writing?
questions.note: Wedge-shaped script on clay tablets, Mesopotamia c. 3200 BC.

questions.question: Which self-governing country first gave women the vote nationally, in 1893?
questions.note: Finland followed in 1906, the UK in 1918/1928, the US in 1920.

questions.question: Which empire did Hernán Cortés conquer?
questions.note: Tenochtitlan fell in 1521. Pizarro conquered the Inca.

questions.question: A historian finds that a ruler's official decree claims a reform was universally welcomed, while private letters describe local resistance. What is the strongest method?

choices.A: Accept the decree because it is official
choices.C: Compare authorship, audience, purpose, and independent evidence before judging the reform's reception
choices.D: Assume the letters represent every resident

questions.note: Source criticism considers perspective and corroborates evidence rather than privileging one source automatically.

questions.question: Why did the enclosure movement contribute to industrial urbanization in Britain?

choices.A: It made agricultural land unproductive everywhere
choices.B: Changes in landholding and farming displaced or redirected some rural labor while agricultural change supported population growth
choices.D: It forced factories to move into villages

questions.note: Enclosure and agricultural change contributed to rural labor mobility, alongside other economic and demographic causes.

questions.question: Which factor best explains why the 1917 Russian Revolutions occurred in a state already weakened by World War I?

choices.B: Military failures, supply crises, and distrust of the monarchy intensified existing social and political tensions
choices.D: The Duma had absolute control over the army

questions.note: Wartime pressures amplified preexisting inequalities and a legitimacy crisis.

questions.question: Why is it misleading to describe the fall of the Western Roman Empire as a single event caused only by invasions?

choices.A: No external groups entered Roman territory
choices.B: Political fragmentation, fiscal and military pressures, and external migrations/interventions interacted over time
choices.D: The eastern empire fell in the same year

questions.note: Historians explain the western empire's transformation through interacting internal and external factors.

questions.question: Which change most directly helped transform World War II into a global war by late 1941?

choices.A: The signing of the Magna Carta
choices.C: Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor and the resulting entry of the United States, alongside the existing European and Asian wars
choices.D: The creation of the United Nations in 1945

questions.note: The United States' entry expanded the scale and resources of the conflict.

questions.question: Which event traditionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire?
questions.note: Odoacer deposed him in 476. The sack was 410, Constantinople 330, Adrianople 378.

questions.question: Which was a direct result of the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.note: Austria-Hungary dated from 1867 and dissolved in 1918.

questions.question: The Berlin Airlift (1948–1949) responded to…

choices.A: The building of the Berlin Wall
choices.D: A Soviet blockade of West Berlin

questions.note: The Wall came later, in 1961.

questions.question: Hammurabi of Babylon is best known for…
questions.note: The Code of Hammurabi, c. 1754 BC.

questions.question: Which revolution created the first republic led by formerly enslaved people?
questions.note: Haiti declared independence in 1804.

questions.question: Two accounts of the same revolution disagree: one emphasizes food prices, the other political exclusion. What evidence would best test whether these causes interacted?

choices.B: Price records, petitions, and accounts showing how economic hardship shaped political mobilization
choices.D: A list of battles without dates

questions.note: Evidence linking material pressures to political action can test interaction between explanations.

questions.question: Why did the 1884–1885 Berlin Conference accelerate European partition of Africa without creating most African borders from scratch at that meeting?

choices.A: It transferred every African kingdom to the United States
choices.B: It established rules among European powers, while conquest, negotiation, and boundary-making continued afterward
choices.C: It granted universal self-government to African states

questions.note: The conference shaped European claims and procedures, but colonization and border formation unfolded over decades.

questions.question: Which interpretation best explains why decolonization after 1945 varied widely in its path?

choices.A: Every colony received independence through identical negotiations
choices.B: Imperial policy, nationalist organization, settler interests, international pressure, and armed conflict differed by region
choices.C: The United Nations directly governed every colony

questions.note: Different local and international conditions produced negotiated transitions in some places and wars in others.

questions.question: A government claims a famine resulted only from drought, but records show grain exports continued during severe shortages. What is the most defensible inference?

choices.B: The records justify investigating policy and distribution alongside environmental conditions, but do not alone prove intent
choices.C: Exports prove the famine was fabricated
choices.D: One document establishes the exact death toll

questions.note: The evidence complicates a single-cause explanation but requires further corroboration.

questions.question: Why did the Cold War produce proxy wars in some regions rather than direct U.S.–Soviet combat?

choices.A: Both powers had no military forces
choices.B: Supporting local allies could advance strategic goals while reducing the risk of direct superpower war
choices.D: Proxy conflicts were always controlled completely by sponsors

questions.note: Proxy warfare allowed competition while managing escalation risk, though local actors retained agency.

questions.question: Which ancient empire built the Royal Road and ruled through satraps?
questions.note: The Achaemenid Persians governed provinces through satraps.

questions.question: What was the outcome of England's Glorious Revolution (1688)?

choices.A: William and Mary replaced James II

questions.note: Charles I's execution was 1649; the Restoration was 1660.

questions.question: Which 19th-century conflict caused the most deaths?
questions.note: Estimates run 20–30 million dead in China, 1850–1864.

questions.question: Why was the Battle of Midway (1942) so significant?
questions.note: The loss crippled Japan's carrier strength.

questions.question: The Emancipation Proclamation applied only to…

choices.C: Areas in rebellion against the Union

questions.note: Slavery was abolished nationwide by the 13th Amendment (1865).

questions.question: A historian argues that the Industrial Revolution was caused by one invention. Which finding would most seriously weaken that thesis?

choices.B: Evidence that productivity rose only where the invention coincided with energy access, capital, labor arrangements, and transport improvements
choices.D: A patent filed in the same century

questions.note: A multi-factor pattern challenges a monocausal account.

questions.question: Why do historians dispute whether the Peace of Westphalia instantly created the modern sovereign-state system?

choices.B: Territorial authority was reinforced, but dynastic, religious, and imperial structures continued and sovereignty developed gradually
choices.C: Europe had no political borders before 1648

questions.note: Westphalia mattered, but the idea of a fully modern state system emerging immediately is too simple.

questions.question: Which evidence most strongly supports the claim that the Atlantic slave trade shaped both African societies and the Americas?

choices.B: Linked shipping records, plantation accounts, demographic evidence, and African political records showing connected effects across regions
choices.C: A modern map without historical data

questions.note: Multiple independent source types can demonstrate interconnected demographic, economic, and political effects.

questions.question: A treaty ends a war but leaves unresolved the causes that produced it. What is the best historical conclusion?

choices.B: The treaty may stop immediate fighting without guaranteeing a durable settlement

questions.note: Ending hostilities and resolving underlying disputes are different outcomes.

questions.question: Which approach best avoids presentism when judging a historical institution?

choices.B: Reconstruct contemporary norms, incentives, and lived effects while distinguishing explanation from moral endorsement
choices.C: Assume people in the past thought exactly as people do now
choices.D: Use only the institution's official justification

questions.note: Contextualization helps explain an institution without requiring its endorsement.

questions.question: The Edict of Nantes (1598) granted rights to…
questions.note: Issued by Henry IV of France for Protestants.

questions.question: Why did Tokugawa Japan adopt its sakoku isolation policy?
questions.note: The shogunate saw missionaries and their converts as a political threat.

questions.question: Which did NOT contribute to the fall of the Western Roman Empire?
questions.note: Islam arose in the 7th century, after 476.

questions.question: Which government held China's UN Security Council seat from 1945 to 1971?
questions.note: UN Resolution 2758 (1971) transferred the seat to the PRC.

questions.question: Why did Napoleon sell the Louisiana Territory in 1803?

choices.D: To end a war with the U.S.

questions.note: After failing to retake Haiti, he needed money for renewed war with Britain.

questions.question: Why are many major cities located near coasts or navigable rivers?

choices.B: They historically reduce transport costs and connect settlements to trade networks
choices.C: Coasts always have the mildest climate

questions.note: Water transport historically moved bulky goods relatively efficiently.

questions.question: Which map projection property is most important when comparing the true relative sizes of countries?

choices.C: Showing all routes as straight lines

questions.note: Equal-area projections preserve relative area, though they distort other properties.

questions.question: Why is it usually cooler at a mountain summit than at its base?

choices.A: Gravity removes all heat from high places
choices.B: Air pressure decreases with altitude, and rising air expands and cools
choices.C: The Sun is farther away by a meaningful amount

questions.note: Lower pressure allows air to expand; the environmental lapse rate generally lowers temperature with altitude.

questions.question: Which country has the most people in South America?
questions.note: Brazil has over 200 million people.

questions.question: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
questions.note: K2 is in the Karakoram.

questions.question: Which desert covers much of northern Africa?
questions.note: The Kalahari is in southern Africa; the Gobi is in Asia.

questions.question: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.note: The Italian peninsula's shape resembles a boot.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.note: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which is the largest country by area?
questions.note: About 17.1 million km²; Canada is second.

questions.question: Which line divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.note: The Prime Meridian divides East and West.

questions.question: A coastal desert lies beside a cold ocean current. How can the current contribute to aridity?

choices.B: It cools lower air, stabilizing the atmosphere and limiting rising moist air
choices.C: It increases evaporation enough to guarantee rain

questions.note: Cold currents can stabilize air and suppress convection, while other factors also shape rainfall.

questions.question: Why can a country's population density be high near a river delta?

choices.A: Deltas are always above flood risk
choices.B: Flat land, fertile sediments, and transport access can support dense settlement despite flood hazards

questions.note: Deltas offer agricultural and transport advantages but also serious environmental risks.

questions.question: What happens to local solar time as longitude increases eastward?

choices.A: It becomes earlier by four minutes per degree
choices.B: It becomes later by roughly four minutes per degree
choices.D: It changes only at the Equator

questions.note: Earth rotates 360° in about 24 hours, or approximately 4 minutes per degree.

questions.question: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean with the…
questions.note: It separates Spain from Morocco.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.note: About 0.44 km²; Monaco is second.

questions.question: Which country does NOT border Germany?
questions.note: Austria and Switzerland separate Germany from Italy.

questions.question: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.note: It sits near the Kenyan border but inside Tanzania.

questions.question: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.note: Toronto is Canada's largest city.

questions.question: Which body of water lies between Saudi Arabia and northeast Africa?
questions.note: The Persian Gulf is on Saudi Arabia's east side.

questions.question: Which U.S. state is the largest by area?
questions.note: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas.

questions.question: Why can two places at the same latitude have very different climates?

choices.B: Elevation, ocean currents, prevailing winds, continentality, and relief modify climate
choices.D: Local geography affects rainfall but never temperature

questions.note: Latitude is important but does not determine climate by itself.

questions.question: A mountain range runs perpendicular to moist prevailing winds. Which pattern is most likely?

choices.A: Equal rainfall on both sides in every season
choices.B: More precipitation on the windward slope and drier conditions in the lee
choices.C: More precipitation only in the rain shadow

questions.note: Orographic lifting promotes windward precipitation; descending air on the leeward side is often drier.

questions.question: Why might a country with a large total area still have relatively little arable land?

choices.A: Area and land quality are unrelated in every case
choices.B: Much of its territory may be desert, mountain, permafrost, or otherwise unsuitable for cultivation
choices.D: Arable land depends only on population

questions.note: Total land area does not equal land suitable for crops.

questions.question: The Danube River empties into which sea?
questions.note: Its delta is on the Romania–Ukraine coast.

questions.question: Which city lies on two continents?
questions.note: The Bosporus splits it between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.note: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as capital in 1960.

questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.note: Over 1,600 m deep, in Siberia.

questions.question: Which north–south range forms much of the conventional Europe–Asia boundary?
questions.note: The Caucasus run east–west further south.

questions.question: What is the largest island that is not a continent?
questions.note: About 2.17 million km²; New Guinea is second.

questions.question: Which river forms much of the U.S.–Mexico border?
questions.note: Called the Río Bravo in Mexico.

questions.question: A river's discharge rises after heavy rain far upstream, while the downstream weather is dry. Which concept best explains this?

choices.A: The downstream climate controls the entire river
choices.B: Discharge integrates water inputs across the upstream drainage basin and travel time
choices.D: River flow is determined only by slope

questions.note: A river responds to basin-wide precipitation, snowmelt, storage, and routing.

questions.question: A city grows rapidly on a delta while groundwater extraction increases. Which coupled risk is especially plausible?

choices.A: Reduced flood risk and rising land
choices.B: Land subsidence that worsens relative sea-level rise and flood exposure
choices.D: A guaranteed increase in river sediment

questions.note: Groundwater withdrawal can compact sediments, causing subsidence and increasing coastal risk.

questions.question: Why do west coasts near 20°–35° latitude often contain deserts?

choices.B: Descending air in subtropical high-pressure belts suppresses clouds, often reinforced by cold currents
choices.C: The Coriolis effect stops all rainfall
choices.D: Mountain ranges are required at every desert

questions.note: Subtropical subsidence is a major desert-forming mechanism; cold currents can intensify dryness.

questions.question: A map shows equal distances from a central point in every direction, but shapes near the edge look stretched. What projection property is likely being prioritized?
questions.note: Azimuthal equidistant projections preserve distance and direction from the center, with distortion increasing outward.

questions.question: Why can a country spanning many longitudes use only one official time zone?

choices.A: Longitude has no relationship to solar time
choices.B: Time zones are political choices, not a physical requirement that each longitude have a separate legal time
choices.C: Earth rotates at different rates over each country

questions.note: Legal time zones can differ from local solar time for administrative and economic reasons.

questions.question: Which line marks the northernmost point where the Sun can be directly overhead?
questions.note: About 23.4° N, reached at the June solstice.

questions.question: Fjords are formed mainly by…
questions.note: Glacial valleys later flooded by the sea.

questions.question: Which country has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean?
questions.note: Venezuela is Caribbean only; Ecuador and Peru are Pacific only.

questions.question: Which 'sea' is actually the world's largest lake?
questions.note: It is landlocked, about 371,000 km².

questions.question: The Strait of Malacca separates which two countries?
questions.note: Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra. The Johor Strait separates Malaysia and Singapore.

questions.question: A population map shows rapid growth around a capital while rural regions lose residents. Which explanation best fits a common pattern in developing economies?

choices.A: Migration must be caused only by climate
choices.B: Jobs, education, services, and investment concentrated in the capital can attract internal migration
choices.C: Rural population loss proves national population is falling
choices.D: Urban growth always reduces total fertility immediately

questions.note: Urban primacy can reflect uneven concentration of economic opportunities and services.

questions.question: Why is the label “natural disaster” sometimes criticized by human geographers?

choices.B: A hazard becomes disastrous through exposure, vulnerability, infrastructure, and preparedness as well as the physical event

questions.note: Social vulnerability shapes how strongly a physical hazard affects people.

questions.question: Two countries share a river, and an upstream dam changes seasonal flow downstream. Which framework is most useful for analyzing the dispute?

choices.B: Transboundary water governance, upstream-downstream dependence, and seasonal flow requirements
choices.C: The countries' distance from the Equator only

questions.note: River management requires considering shared basins, allocation, ecology, and political institutions.

questions.question: Why can the same amount of rainfall produce more flash flooding in an urbanized watershed than in a forested one?

choices.A: Concrete absorbs more water than soil
choices.B: Impervious surfaces speed runoff and reduce infiltration, shortening the time water reaches channels
choices.D: Urban drainage always stores all rain

questions.note: Impervious cover often increases runoff volume and peak discharge.

questions.question: A country has high GDP per capita but low access to clean water in remote areas. What does this suggest about using GDP per capita alone?

choices.A: It precisely measures every household's welfare
choices.B: National averages can conceal regional inequality and gaps in basic services
choices.C: It proves the GDP figure is false
choices.D: It means water access is unrelated to development

questions.note: Aggregate income does not show how resources and services are distributed.

questions.question: Which country lies entirely south of the Equator?
questions.note: Kenya, Indonesia, and Colombia all straddle the Equator.

questions.question: Which major river flows mostly northward?
questions.note: It flows north to the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Which country's capital lies on the Danube?
questions.note: Budapest. Prague is on the Vltava, Warsaw the Vistula, Bucharest the Dâmbovița.

questions.question: Which is the largest country located entirely in Europe?
questions.note: About 603,000 km². Russia, Kazakhstan, and Turkey span two continents.

questions.question: The point at 0° latitude, 0° longitude lies in which body of water?
questions.note: Off the coast of West Africa.

questions.question: A region becomes warmer while annual precipitation remains constant, but drought risk increases. Which explanation is strongest?

choices.B: Higher evaporative demand can dry soils and reduce water availability even without lower rainfall
choices.C: Drought is defined only by rainfall totals
choices.D: Warmer air always produces more local rain

questions.note: Drought can intensify through greater evapotranspiration and soil-moisture loss.

questions.question: A map uses a conformal projection. Which claim can safely be made?

choices.A: All areas are shown in correct relative size
choices.B: Local angles and shapes are preserved, but area and distance may be distorted

questions.note: Conformal projections preserve local angles, not all geometric properties.

questions.question: Why can a small island's freshwater supply be vulnerable even if annual rainfall is high?

choices.B: Limited storage, rapid runoff, seasonal variability, and saltwater intrusion can constrain usable freshwater
choices.D: High rainfall guarantees year-round drinking water

questions.note: Rainfall totals alone do not determine accessible freshwater storage and quality.

questions.question: A glacier-fed river's peak flow shifts earlier in the year as temperatures rise. What is a plausible long-term concern?

choices.A: Peak flow must continue increasing forever
choices.B: Earlier melt may temporarily raise early-season flow but eventually reduce late-season water as glacier storage shrinks
choices.D: The timing of melt cannot affect agriculture

questions.note: Glacier retreat can shift seasonal runoff and reduce dry-season reliability.

questions.question: Why can the same coastal storm create different damage in two towns with similar wind speeds?

choices.B: Elevation, coastal shape, building standards, warning systems, and social vulnerability differ
choices.C: Storm surge is identical on every coastline
choices.D: Population size is the only relevant variable

questions.note: Exposure and vulnerability strongly shape impacts beyond storm intensity.

questions.question: Which country borders both the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf?
questions.note: Iran's north coast is on the Caspian, its south on the Gulf.

questions.question: Which country's territory is the first to enter each new calendar day?
questions.note: Kiribati's Line Islands use UTC+14.

questions.question: Besides Uganda, which two countries border Lake Victoria?
questions.note: Tanzania holds about half the lake.

questions.question: Which country has NO Mediterranean coastline?
questions.note: Portugal faces only the Atlantic; Slovenia and Bosnia have short Adriatic coasts.

questions.question: Going straight through Earth's center from Manila, you would surface in…
questions.note: Manila's antipode is near 14.6° S, 59° W, in central South America.

questions.question: A student doubles the mass of a cart while keeping its net force constant. According to Newton's second law, what happens to its acceleration?
questions.note: Since a = F/m, doubling mass at constant net force halves acceleration.

questions.question: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon in the same room?

choices.A: The metal must have a lower temperature
choices.B: Metal conducts heat away from the hand faster than wood

questions.note: Thermal conductivity changes the rate of heat transfer, not necessarily the object's temperature.

questions.question: A solution changes blue litmus paper to red. What can be concluded most directly?
questions.note: Blue litmus turning red indicates acidic conditions.

questions.question: Which part of an animal cell holds most of its DNA?
questions.note: Ribosomes build proteins; the membrane encloses the cell.

questions.question: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.note: Inertia alone would send planets off in straight lines.

questions.question: At sea level, water boils at what temperature?
questions.note: Equal to 212 °F.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.note: Jupiter is over 300 times Earth's mass.

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.note: Diamond is 10 on the Mohs scale.

questions.question: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.note: Babies have about 270–300 that fuse over time.

questions.question: What kind of animal is a whale?
questions.note: Whales breathe air and nurse their young.

questions.question: A plant is kept in darkness for several days but is watered normally. Which process is directly limited first?
questions.note: Light is required for photosynthesis, although respiration continues.

questions.question: Why does a sealed syringe become harder to compress as its plunger is pushed inward?

choices.B: The same gas occupies less volume, increasing pressure through more frequent particle-wall collisions
choices.C: The gas loses all kinetic energy
choices.D: The number of gas particles increases automatically

questions.note: Compression reduces volume and raises pressure for a fixed amount of gas at roughly constant temperature.

questions.question: A 12 V battery is connected across a 6 Ω resistor. What current flows through the resistor?
questions.note: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 12/6 = 2 A.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.note: From Latin 'natrium'. S is sulfur.

questions.question: Through which material does sound travel fastest?
questions.note: Sound is fastest in solids and cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: Which blood cells fight infection?
questions.note: Red cells carry oxygen; platelets help clotting.

questions.question: Which planet has the hottest surface?
questions.note: Venus's thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat (~465 °C), hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a negative charge?
questions.note: Protons and positrons are positive; neutrons are neutral.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms when magma cools?
questions.note: Clastic rocks are a kind of sedimentary rock.

questions.question: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.note: Neutral is pH 7.

questions.question: A ball is thrown straight upward. At its highest point, ignoring air resistance, which statement is correct?

choices.A: Velocity and acceleration are both zero
choices.B: Velocity is zero but acceleration is downward
choices.C: Velocity is upward and acceleration is zero
choices.D: Velocity and acceleration are both upward

questions.note: The instantaneous velocity is zero at the top, but gravity still accelerates the ball downward.

questions.question: A mutation changes one DNA base but does not change the amino acid sequence. Which explanation is most likely?

choices.A: The genetic code is degenerate, so multiple codons can specify the same amino acid

questions.note: A synonymous mutation can change a codon without changing the encoded amino acid.

questions.question: Why does adding a catalyst increase reaction rate without changing the reaction's equilibrium constant?

choices.A: It raises the energy of all products
choices.B: It lowers activation barriers for forward and reverse reactions but does not change the equilibrium energy difference
choices.C: It changes the chemical formula of the reactants

questions.note: A catalyst changes kinetics, not the thermodynamic equilibrium constant at a given temperature.

questions.question: Which element has atomic number 6?
questions.note: Boron is 5, nitrogen 7, oxygen 8.

questions.question: In which atmospheric layer is the ozone layer found?
questions.note: Roughly 15–35 km up.

questions.question: What type of energy does a stretched rubber band store?
questions.note: Released as kinetic energy when let go.

questions.question: What is the shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.note: Described by Watson and Crick in 1953.

questions.question: Which planet has the shortest day?
questions.note: Jupiter rotates in about 10 hours; Saturn in about 10.7.

questions.question: Which vitamin does your skin make in sunlight?
questions.note: UVB light triggers vitamin D production.

questions.question: Which of these is a noble gas?
questions.note: Noble gases (group 18) are very unreactive.

questions.question: A v–t graph is a straight line with a negative slope, crossing the time axis from positive to negative velocity. What does the signed area over the full interval represent?

choices.B: Net displacement, with areas below the axis counted negatively

questions.note: The integral of velocity over time is displacement; total distance uses the magnitude of velocity.

questions.question: A population is in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium with recessive phenotype frequency 0.09. What is the expected heterozygote frequency?
A gas is heated at constant pressure. What happens to its volume under the ideal-gas model?

choices.B: It increases in proportion to absolute temperature
choices.D: It becomes inversely proportional to temperature

questions.note: Charles's law states V/T is constant at fixed pressure and amount of gas.

questions.question: In a controlled experiment, both the treatment group and control group improve equally. What is the strongest conclusion?

choices.B: The improvement alone does not demonstrate a treatment effect; placebo effects, time, or other factors may explain it
choices.D: The sample proves no treatment could ever work

questions.note: The treatment's effect must be judged relative to the control, not just pre-post change.

questions.question: Two resistors, 4 Ω and 6 Ω, are connected in series to a 20 V ideal source. What is the voltage across the 6 Ω resistor?
questions.note: The total resistance is 10 Ω, current is 2 A, and the 6 Ω resistor has 12 V across it.

questions.question: What happens to water's boiling point at high altitude?
questions.note: Lower air pressure lets water boil at a lower temperature.

questions.question: Why is the daytime sky blue?
questions.note: Rayleigh scattering affects shorter wavelengths most.

questions.question: In a simple series circuit, if one bulb burns out, the other bulbs…
questions.note: A series circuit has only one path; a break stops all current.

questions.question: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.note: Rust is a new substance (iron oxide). The others are physical changes.

questions.question: What mainly causes Earth's seasons?
questions.note: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January.

questions.question: A rock weighs 30 N in air and 20 N when fully submerged in water. Assuming the buoyant force equals the weight of displaced water, what is the rock's density relative to water?
questions.note: The rock's weight is 30 N and buoyant force is 10 N; density ratio is 30/10 = 3.

questions.question: A solution has pH 3 and another has pH 5. How do their hydrogen-ion concentrations compare?

choices.A: The pH 3 solution has 2 times as much
choices.B: The pH 3 solution has 100 times as much
choices.C: The pH 5 solution has 100 times as much

questions.note: Each pH unit corresponds to a tenfold change in hydrogen-ion concentration.

questions.question: A species is moved to a new environment where it has no predators and abundant food. Its population grows rapidly, then levels off. What best explains the leveling?

choices.B: Density-dependent limits such as competition and resource constraints become stronger near carrying capacity
choices.D: The environment now has infinite resources

questions.note: Population growth slows as limiting factors intensify near carrying capacity.

questions.question: Light enters water from air at an oblique angle. Which pair of changes occurs?

choices.B: Speed decreases and wavelength decreases while frequency stays constant
choices.C: Frequency decreases and speed stays constant
choices.D: Wavelength stays constant and frequency rises

questions.note: Frequency is unchanged at the boundary; lower speed in water means shorter wavelength.

questions.question: A planet's orbital radius around the same star increases. Under Kepler's third law, what happens to its orbital period?
questions.note: For planets orbiting the same star, a larger semimajor axis corresponds to a longer period.

questions.question: Two 6-ohm resistors connected in parallel have a total resistance of…
Why do astronauts float aboard the International Space Station?

choices.A: They are in continuous free fall
choices.B: There is no gravity in orbit

questions.note: Gravity at ISS height is still about 90% of surface gravity.

questions.question: B is dominant over b. If both parents are Bb, what is the chance a child is bb?
questions.note: Punnett square: BB, Bb, bB, bb — one in four.

questions.question: As a siren moves away from you, its pitch sounds…
questions.note: The Doppler effect stretches the sound waves.

questions.question: Why don't antibiotics cure the common cold?
questions.note: Antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses.

questions.question: A 2.0 kg cart moving at 6.0 m/s experiences a constant 5.0 N force opposite its motion for 1.0 s. What is its speed after that second?
questions.note: Acceleration is −5/2 = −2.5 m/s²; velocity changes from 6.0 to 3.5 m/s.

questions.question: A weak monoprotic acid has Ka = 1.0×10⁻⁵. Using [H⁺]≈√(KaC), compare 0.10 M and 0.0010 M solutions. What is the approximate pH difference?

choices.B: 1 unit, with the dilute solution higher
choices.C: 2 units, with the dilute solution higher

questions.note: A 100-fold decrease in concentration lowers [H⁺] by about tenfold, increasing pH by about one.

questions.question: A projectile is launched from level ground at speed v and angle θ. Which adjustment preserves maximum height but generally changes range?

choices.B: Keep v sin θ constant while changing θ
choices.C: Keep v cos θ constant while changing θ
choices.D: Change θ to 45° without changing v

questions.note: Maximum height depends on (v sin θ)², while range also depends on the horizontal component and flight time.

questions.question: An enzyme's activity falls sharply above a certain temperature. Which explanation is strongest?

choices.A: The reaction has run out of atoms
choices.B: Heat disrupts the enzyme's structure, altering the active site's shape
choices.C: Higher temperature always lowers molecular motion
choices.D: The enzyme becomes a different element

questions.note: Excessive heat can denature the protein and reduce substrate binding/catalysis.

questions.question: A bulb is added in parallel to two identical bulbs connected to an ideal battery. What happens to current through each original bulb?

choices.A: It decreases because total current rises
choices.B: It remains unchanged because each branch still has the battery voltage
choices.C: It doubles because there are three branches

questions.note: In an ideal parallel circuit, each branch receives the same source voltage.

questions.question: If Earth had no Moon, ocean tides would…
questions.note: The Sun would still cause tides, about half as strong.

questions.question: An isotope's half-life is 10 years. What fraction remains after 30 years?
Which element most readily forms a +1 ion?
questions.note: Alkali metals lose one electron. Mg forms +2; Cl and O form negative ions.

questions.question: If a car's speed doubles, its kinetic energy becomes…
questions.note: KE = ½mv², so doubling v quadruples KE.

questions.question: Why does air in the lower atmosphere get colder as you climb, despite being nearer the Sun?

choices.B: It is heated mainly from the ground

questions.note: Sunlight warms the surface, which warms the air above it.

questions.question: A jacket costs $80 and is discounted by 25%. What is the sale price?
questions.note: 25% of $80 is $20, so the sale price is $60.

questions.question: If 3x − 7 = 11, what is x?
questions.note: Add 7 to get 3x=18, then divide by 3.

questions.question: A rectangle has perimeter 30 cm and length 9 cm. What is its width?
questions.note: 2(L+W)=30, so L+W=15 and W=6.

questions.question: What is 3/4 written as a decimal?
How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.note: Pentagon 5, heptagon 7, octagon 8.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a square with 9 cm sides?
questions.note: 4 × 9 = 36. 81 cm² would be the area.

questions.question: Which of these is a prime number?
What is 2³?
What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
questions.note: Always 180° in flat (Euclidean) geometry.

questions.question: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for 8 servings. How much flour is needed for 20 servings at the same ratio?
questions.note: Scale by 20/8: 3×2.5=7.5 cups.

questions.question: A fair coin is flipped twice. What is the probability of getting exactly one head?
questions.note: The outcomes HT and TH are 2 of 4 equally likely outcomes.

questions.question: The mean of five numbers is 12. Four numbers sum to 41. What is the fifth number?
questions.note: The total must be 5×12=60, so the fifth number is 19.

questions.question: A ₱1,200 item is 15% off. What is the sale price?
Solve: 3x + 5 = 20
What is the average of 4, 8, 10, and 18?
How many minutes are in 3.5 hours?
Which fraction is largest?
Using π ≈ 22/7, what is the circumference of a circle with radius 7?
questions.note: 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44. 154 would be the area.

questions.question: A tank is 3/5 full. After 24 liters are added, it is 3/4 full. What is the tank's capacity?
questions.note: The increase is 3/4−3/5=3/20 of capacity; 24÷(3/20)=160 L.

questions.question: A line passes through (2, 7) and (6, 19). What is its y-intercept?
questions.note: Slope=(19−7)/(6−2)=3, so y=3x+1; intercept is 1.

questions.question: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue marbles. One marble is chosen at random. What is the probability it is not blue?
questions.note: There are 4 red marbles out of 10, so the probability is 4/10=2/5.

questions.question: Solve: 2(x − 3) = x + 4
What comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, …?
questions.note: Differences grow 4, 6, 8, 10, then 12.

questions.question: A right triangle has legs 9 and 12. How long is the hypotenuse?
What is the least common multiple of 12 and 18?
questions.note: 6 is the GCF; 36 is the smallest common multiple.

questions.question: What is 0.25 × 0.4?
How many diagonals does a pentagon have?
Simplify (x²)³
questions.note: Multiply exponents: 2 × 3 = 6.

questions.question: A price increases by 20% and then decreases by 20%. What is the net change from the original price?
questions.note: Multiplying by 1.2 and then 0.8 gives 0.96 of the original price.

questions.question: A quadratic has roots 2 and −5 and leading coefficient 3. Which is its expanded form?
A right triangle has legs 9 and 12. What is the radius of its circumcircle?
questions.note: The hypotenuse is 15, and the circumradius of a right triangle is half the hypotenuse, 7.5.

questions.question: A line has slope 2 and passes through (−1, 4). Which equation represents it?
questions.note: Using y−4=2(x+1) gives y=2x+6.

questions.question: A fair six-sided die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
questions.note: Six of the 36 ordered outcomes sum to 7, so the probability is 1/6.

questions.question: A rectangle's length is doubled and its width tripled. Its area becomes…
If f(x) = 3x − 2, what is f(f(2))?
In how many different orders can 4 people stand in a line?
What is the median of 7, 3, 9, 1, 12, 5?
What is the slope of the line through (2, 3) and (6, 11)?
Two cards are drawn without replacement from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability both are aces?
A quadratic function has vertex (3, −4) and passes through (1, 4). What is its equation in vertex form?
questions.note: Substitute (1,4): 4=a(−2)²−4, so a=2.

questions.question: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours and another in 4 hours. How long do they take together, assuming constant rates?
questions.note: Combined rate is 1/6+1/4=5/12 tank per hour; time is 12/5=2.4 hours.

questions.question: A circle's radius increases by 10%. By what percentage does its area increase?
questions.note: Area scales with radius squared: 1.1²=1.21, a 21% increase.

questions.question: If f(x)=x²−4x and g(x)=2x+1, what is f(g(1))?
What is the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 50?
After a 25% discount, a shirt costs ₱600. What was the original price?
How many three-digit numbers are divisible by 5?
What is log₁₀(1000) + log₁₀(0.01)?
What is the smaller angle between a clock's hands at 3:30?
questions.note: Hour hand at 105°, minute hand at 180°.

questions.question: A fair die is rolled four times. What is the probability of getting at least one 6?
questions.note: Use the complement: 1−(5/6)^4 = 671/1296.

questions.question: How many distinct 4-person committees can be chosen from 9 people?
questions.note: The number is C(9,4)=126.

questions.question: For x>0, f(x)=x^x. Which expression equals f′(x)?
questions.note: Write x^x=e^(x ln x); differentiating gives x^x(ln x+1).

questions.question: A polynomial has roots −2, 1, and 4 and leading coefficient 2. What is its constant term?
questions.note: The polynomial is 2(x+2)(x−1)(x−4); the constant term is 2·2·(−1)·(−4)=16.

questions.question: A function satisfies f′(x)=3x²−4 and f(0)=5. What is f(2)?
questions.note: Integrating gives f(x)=x³−4x+5, so f(2)=5.

questions.question: Why was the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 relevant to Filipino reformist thought?

choices.C: It abolished the galleon trade in 1565

questions.question: Who became President of the Commonwealth when it was established in 1935?

questions.question: Why did the Tejeros Convention deepen conflict within the revolutionary movement?

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes the First Philippine Republic from the Commonwealth established in 1935?

choices.A: The First Republic emerged from the 1898–1899 revolution; the Commonwealth was a transitional government under U.S. sovereignty
choices.B: Both were created by the 1987 Constitution
choices.C: The Commonwealth preceded the Spanish colonial period
choices.D: The First Republic was established by Japan in 1943

questions.question: Why did the Philippine-American War continue after the Treaty of Paris?

choices.A: The treaty recognized an independent Philippine government accepted by all sides
choices.B: Filipino nationalists rejected U.S. sovereignty, while the treaty transferred Spain's claim without Filipino consent
choices.D: The war was fought only over trade tariffs

questions.note: The treaty was negotiated between Spain and the United States, not the Filipino revolutionary government.

questions.question: Which revolt was the longest in Philippine history?
questions.note: Bohol, 1744–1829: about 85 years.

questions.question: Where was Philippine independence proclaimed on June 12, 1898?
questions.note: At Aguinaldo's house in Kawit.

questions.question: The Malolos Constitution established which government?
questions.note: Promulgated January 1899.

questions.question: Who composed the music of the Philippine national anthem?
questions.note: Palma wrote the Spanish lyrics; Agoncillo sewed the flag.

questions.question: Who succeeded Manuel Quezon as Commonwealth President in 1944?
questions.note: Laurel headed the Japanese-sponsored Second Republic.

questions.question: Who was the first American civil governor of the Philippines?
questions.note: Appointed in 1901; later U.S. President.

questions.question: Sultan Kudarat led which sultanate against Spanish expansion?

questions.question: Why is the Pact of Biak-na-Bato not equivalent to a treaty granting Philippine independence?

choices.A: It was a truce involving exile and promised payments, not international recognition of independence
choices.B: It transferred sovereignty from Spain to the United States
choices.D: It abolished the Katipunan before the revolution began

questions.note: The pact paused conflict and arranged exile; it did not establish sovereign independence.

questions.question: Which factor helps explain why the 1935 Constitution included a transition toward independence rather than immediate full sovereignty?

choices.A: The Philippines was already fully independent in 1935
choices.B: The Commonwealth operated under a U.S. framework that set a transition period toward independence
choices.C: The constitution was written under Japanese occupation
choices.D: The constitution prohibited any future republic

questions.note: The Commonwealth was designed as a transitional government under U.S. sovereignty.

questions.question: Why is the 1973 Constitution's political context important when evaluating the Marcos government's claim of constitutional legitimacy?

choices.A: Constitutional texts can be evaluated without considering how they were adopted
choices.B: The constitution was adopted during martial-law rule, raising questions about coercion, ratification, and concentration of power
choices.C: It was drafted before the Philippine Revolution
choices.D: It abolished the presidency before Marcos took office

questions.note: The conditions of adoption and implementation are central to assessing constitutional legitimacy.

questions.question: Why did the 1986 People Power Revolution lead to a major constitutional transition?

choices.A: It restored the 1935 Constitution without changes
choices.B: The new government moved to replace the Marcos-era constitutional order, culminating in the 1987 Constitution

questions.note: The post-EDSA government undertook a new constitutional process, resulting in the 1987 Constitution.

questions.question: What is the strongest reason historians compare the Propaganda Movement with the revolutionary movement without treating them as identical?

choices.A: Both had exactly the same goals and methods
choices.B: They shared opposition to colonial abuses, but differed in strategies, organizations, and willingness to pursue armed revolution
choices.C: The Propaganda Movement began after the 1986 revolution
choices.D: The Katipunan was a newspaper published in Madrid

questions.note: There were connections and overlap, but reformist advocacy and revolutionary organizing were distinct approaches.

questions.question: What happened at the Battle of Manila Bay in 1898?

questions.question: When did Rizal write 'Mi Último Adiós'?

choices.B: On the eve of his execution

questions.question: A colonial report describes a revolt as criminal disorder, while a local account frames it as resistance to abuses. How should a historian assess the disagreement?

choices.A: Accept the colonial report as neutral because it is official
choices.B: Compare each source's purpose, position, corroboration, and the specific grievances documented
choices.C: Assume the local account is automatically accurate
choices.D: Ignore both and use only modern summaries

questions.note: Source criticism weighs perspective and evidence rather than treating either source as automatically definitive.

questions.question: Why did the Malolos Congress matter to the First Philippine Republic beyond symbolic representation?

choices.A: It helped formulate constitutional institutions and laws for a revolutionary government
choices.B: It was the body that signed the Treaty of Paris for Spain
choices.C: It governed the Philippines during the 1986 transition
choices.D: It served as the Katipunan's secret initiation council

questions.note: The congress participated in constitutional state-building for the republic.

questions.question: Why did the Hare–Hawes–Cutting Act become controversial among Filipino leaders including Manuel L. Quezon?

choices.A: It granted immediate independence without conditions
choices.B: Disagreements centered on its provisions, including military bases and trade arrangements, and the terms of the transition
choices.C: It returned the Philippines to Spain

questions.note: Filipino leaders disagreed over the act's conditions and implications for sovereignty.

questions.question: What does the conflicting historical dating of the “Cry” events of August 1896 most clearly demonstrate?

choices.B: Historical events can be remembered and documented differently, requiring comparison of testimonies and definitions of the event
choices.D: Only the date in a modern textbook matters

questions.question: Why is the 1872 Cavite Mutiny often discussed alongside the execution of GOMBURZA and the rise of reformist nationalism?

choices.A: The three are unrelated events separated by centuries
choices.B: The colonial response and executions became a catalyst in later critiques of Spanish rule and racial injustice

questions.question: How did the opening of the Suez Canal (1869) affect Filipino nationalism?

choices.B: It sped the arrival of liberal ideas

questions.question: Which comparison between the Pact of Biak-na-Bato and the Treaty of Paris is most accurate?

choices.A: Both recognized Philippine independence in international law

questions.question: How did the U.S. colonial period differ institutionally from Spanish rule, while still maintaining colonial control?

choices.B: It expanded U.S.-style public education and representative institutions while ultimate sovereignty remained American

questions.question: What is the most careful conclusion when official records and oral histories disagree about a local resistance movement?

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Through which material does sound travel fastest?
questions.note: Sound is fastest in solids and cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which blood cells fight infection?
questions.note: Red cells carry oxygen; platelets help clotting.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which planet has the hottest surface?
questions.note: Venus's thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat (~465 °C), hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which subatomic particle has a negative charge?
questions.note: Protons and positrons are positive; neutrons are neutral.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which type of rock forms when magma cools?
questions.note: Clastic rocks are a kind of sedimentary rock.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.note: Neutral is pH 7.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
questions.note: Both occur together; light arrives almost instantly.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which gas forms when baking soda reacts with vinegar?
questions.note: An acid–base reaction releases CO₂ bubbles.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.note: Veins return blood to the heart.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which element has atomic number 6?
questions.note: Boron is 5, nitrogen 7, oxygen 8.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: In which atmospheric layer is the ozone layer found?
questions.note: Roughly 15–35 km up.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What type of energy does a stretched rubber band store?
questions.note: Released as kinetic energy when let go.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.note: Described by Watson and Crick in 1953.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which planet has the shortest day?
questions.note: Jupiter rotates in about 10 hours; Saturn in about 10.7.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which vitamin does your skin make in sunlight?
questions.note: UVB light triggers vitamin D production.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which of these is a noble gas?
questions.note: Noble gases (group 18) are very unreactive.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What causes the Moon's phases?

choices.D: Our changing view of its lit half

questions.note: Earth's shadow on the Moon is a lunar eclipse, not a phase.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Compared with on Earth, an astronaut's mass on the Moon is…?
questions.note: Weight drops to about one-sixth; mass does not change.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Ignoring air resistance, a bowling ball and a tennis ball are dropped together. Which lands first?
questions.note: Gravity accelerates all objects equally.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why does ice float on liquid water?

choices.D: It is less dense than water

questions.note: Water expands when it freezes.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which process releases energy from glucose inside cells?
questions.note: It takes place mainly in mitochondria.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What happens to water's boiling point at high altitude?
questions.note: Lower air pressure lets water boil at a lower temperature.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why is the daytime sky blue?
questions.note: Rayleigh scattering affects shorter wavelengths most.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: In a simple series circuit, if one bulb burns out, the other bulbs…?
questions.note: A series circuit has only one path; a break stops all current.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.note: Rust is a new substance (iron oxide). The others are physical changes.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What mainly causes Earth's seasons?
questions.note: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: A ball thrown straight up reaches its highest point. Its acceleration there is…?
questions.note: Velocity is zero at the top, but gravity still accelerates it.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which blood type is the universal donor for red blood cells?
questions.note: AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: At the same room temperature, why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden one?
questions.note: Both are the same temperature; metal draws heat from your hand faster.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What happens to an animal cell placed in very salty water?
questions.note: Osmosis moves water out toward the saltier side.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which planet is less dense than water?
questions.note: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 g/cm³.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Two 6-ohm resistors connected in parallel have a total resistance of…?
Scientific knowledge check: Why do astronauts float aboard the International Space Station?

choices.A: They are in continuous free fall
choices.D: There is no gravity in orbit

questions.note: Gravity at ISS height is still about 90% of surface gravity.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: B is dominant over b. If both parents are Bb, what is the chance a child is bb?
questions.note: Punnett square: BB, Bb, bB, bb — one in four.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: As a siren moves away from you, its pitch sounds…?
questions.note: The Doppler effect stretches the sound waves.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why don't antibiotics cure the common cold?
questions.note: Antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: A rock weighs 30 N in air and 20 N fully underwater. Its density is how many times water's?
questions.note: Buoyant force = 10 N = weight of equal-volume water, so 30 ÷ 10 = 3.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: When light passes from air into water, its speed and wavelength…?
questions.note: Frequency stays constant, so wavelength shrinks with speed.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Why is it accelerating?
questions.note: Acceleration is any change in velocity, including direction.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which is the strongest evidence the continents were once joined?
questions.note: Fossils like Mesosaurus appear in both South America and Africa.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which has more total thermal energy?
questions.note: Temperature is average energy per particle; the tub has far more water.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: If Earth had no Moon, ocean tides would…?
questions.note: The Sun would still cause tides, about half as strong.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: An isotope's half-life is 10 years. What fraction remains after 30 years?
Scientific knowledge check: Which element most readily forms a +1 ion?
questions.note: Alkali metals lose one electron. Mg forms +2; Cl and O form negative ions.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: If a car's speed doubles, its kinetic energy becomes…?
questions.note: KE = ½mv², so doubling v quadruples KE.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Why does air in the lower atmosphere get colder as you climb, despite being nearer the Sun?

choices.B: It is heated mainly from the ground

questions.note: Sunlight warms the surface, which warms the air above it.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.note: H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.note: Venus is second.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.note: Plants release oxygen as a by-product.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which part of an animal cell holds most of its DNA?

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.note: Inertia alone would send planets off in straight lines.

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: At sea level, water boils at what temperature?

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What is the hardest natural substance?

questions.question: Scientific knowledge check: What kind of animal is a whale?

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who wrote the novel 'Noli Me Tangere'?
