questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who was the Supremo of the Katipunan when the Revolution began in 1896?
questions.note: Rizal was never a Katipunan member.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: On what date is Philippine Independence Day celebrated?
questions.note: December 30 is Rizal Day.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which explorer reached the Philippines for Spain in 1521?
questions.note: Legazpi came in 1565; Villalobos in 1543.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Whose forces defeated Magellan at the Battle of Mactan?
questions.note: Humabon of Cebu was Magellan's ally.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which country took control of the Philippines after Spain?
questions.note: Through the 1898 Treaty of Paris.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who is recognized as the first President of the Philippines?
questions.note: President of the First (Malolos) Republic, 1899.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: The 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution removed which president?
questions.note: Estrada was ousted by EDSA II in 2001.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: The Philippines was named after which Spanish king?
questions.note: Villalobos named the islands for the future Philip II.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who was the first female President of the Philippines?
Philippine history challenge: Where was José Rizal executed in 1896?
questions.note: Bagumbayan is today's Luneta (Rizal Park). He was held in Fort Santiago.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which Rizal novel is the sequel to 'Noli Me Tangere'?
questions.note: Published in 1891 in Ghent.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which was the first permanent Spanish settlement in the Philippines?
questions.note: Founded by Legazpi in 1565; Manila followed in 1571.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: The Galleon Trade connected Manila with which port?
questions.note: It ran from 1565 to 1815.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: In what year did Ferdinand Marcos declare martial law?
questions.note: 1965 = first elected; 1981 = martial law lifted.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which general died defending Tirad Pass in 1899?
questions.note: His stand covered Aguinaldo's retreat.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which group published 'La Solidaridad' in Spain?
questions.note: Reformists including Rizal, del Pilar, and López Jaena.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which treaty transferred the Philippines from Spain to the United States?
questions.note: Signed December 1898.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: The Bataan Death March took place during which period?
questions.note: April 1942, after the fall of Bataan.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who became President of the Commonwealth when it was established in 1935?
questions.note: Quezon defeated Aguinaldo in the 1935 election.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who is called the 'Brains of the Katipunan'?
questions.note: Mabini is the 'Brains of the Revolution'.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: What act symbolized the Cry of Pugad Lawin in 1896?
questions.note: Katipuneros tore their community tax certificates.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Gomez, Burgos, and Zamora were executed in 1872 following which event?
questions.note: Spanish authorities blamed the three priests for the mutiny.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which revolt was the longest in Philippine history?
questions.note: Bohol, 1744–1829: about 85 years.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Where was Philippine independence proclaimed on June 12, 1898?
questions.note: At Aguinaldo's house in Kawit.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: The Malolos Constitution established which government?
questions.note: Promulgated January 1899.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who composed the music of the Philippine national anthem?
questions.note: Palma wrote the Spanish lyrics; Agoncillo sewed the flag.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who succeeded Manuel Quezon as Commonwealth President in 1944?
questions.note: Laurel headed the Japanese-sponsored Second Republic.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Who was the first American civil governor of the Philippines?
questions.note: Appointed in 1901; later U.S. President.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Sultan Kudarat led which sultanate against Spanish expansion?
questions.note: He ruled in the 17th century in Mindanao.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: What is the earliest known written document found in the Philippines?
questions.note: Dated to 900 AD. The Calatagan Pot is centuries later; the other two are Spanish-era.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Why did the Tejeros Convention (1897) cause a crisis?
questions.note: His election as Director of the Interior was challenged.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: The Pact of Biak-na-Bato (1897) provided for…?

choices.D: A truce and exile to Hong Kong

questions.note: Aguinaldo and others left for Hong Kong in exchange for payment.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which 1899 incident began the Philippine–American War?
questions.note: February 4, 1899. Balangiga was 1901; Manila Bay (1898) was against Spain.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which U.S. law set a 10-year transition to Philippine independence?
questions.note: Passed 1934; the Jones Law (1916) only promised eventual independence.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: What happened at the Battle of Manila Bay in 1898?
questions.note: Commodore Dewey's victory, May 1, 1898.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Huk leader Luis Taruc surrendered in 1954 during whose presidency?
questions.note: Magsaysay fought the Huks as Quirino's defense secretary, then as president.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which president is associated with the 'Filipino First' policy?
questions.note: It favored Filipino-owned businesses.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which 1983 event most directly fueled the movement leading to EDSA?
questions.note: Aquino was killed at the Manila airport on August 21, 1983.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: When did Rizal write 'Mi Último Adiós'?

choices.B: On a ship bound for Cuba
choices.D: On the eve of his execution

questions.note: Smuggled out of Fort Santiago in an alcohol stove.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Rizal was exiled to Dapitan soon after founding which organization?
questions.note: Founded July 1892; he was arrested days later.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: The British occupied Manila (1762–1764) as part of which war?
questions.note: Spain joined France against Britain in 1762.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which Spanish policy moved scattered natives into towns 'under the bells'?
questions.note: Centralized settlements around a church.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Whose 1902 surrender is often seen as ending organized resistance in the Philippine–American War?
questions.note: Sakay kept fighting until 1906, but as a smaller movement.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: The postwar 'parity rights' amendment gave Americans…?
questions.note: Required by the Bell Trade Act; ratified in 1947.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: In precolonial Tagalog society, which class served others because of debt or obligation?
questions.note: Maginoo = nobility; maharlika = warrior class; timawa = freemen.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which president signed the 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty with the United States?
questions.note: Signed in August 1951.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which institution's call over Radio Veritas drew crowds to EDSA in 1986?
questions.note: Cardinal Jaime Sin urged people to support the defectors.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: When Legazpi's forces arrived in Manila Bay in 1570–1571, who ruled Tondo?
questions.note: Sulayman and Matanda ruled Maynila; Humabon ruled Cebu.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: How did the opening of the Suez Canal (1869) affect Filipino nationalism?

choices.A: It sped the arrival of liberal ideas

questions.note: Faster travel let ilustrados study in Europe and bring ideas home.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which colonial system forced natives to sell produce to the government at set prices?
questions.note: Polo y servicio was forced labor; encomienda granted tribute rights.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Quezon opposed the Hare–Hawes–Cutting Act mainly over which provision?
questions.note: He then secured the Tydings–McDuffie Act in 1934.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which correctly orders these Revolution-era events, earliest first?

choices.A: Rizal's execution, Pugad Lawin, Biak-na-Bato, Kawit
choices.B: Pugad Lawin, Rizal's execution, Biak-na-Bato, Kawit

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: How did Spanish authorities learn of the Katipunan in August 1896?
questions.note: Patiño told a friar, who alerted the authorities.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which law provided for the Philippine Assembly, first convened in 1907?
questions.note: The Jones Law (1916) later created an elected Senate.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: What was Andrés de Urdaneta's key contribution to the Legazpi expedition?

choices.A: Finding the return route to Mexico

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which pairing of a Katipunan faction and its leading figure is correct?
questions.note: Magdiwang was led by Mariano Álvarez.

questions.question: Philippine history challenge: Which president moved Independence Day from July 4 to June 12?
questions.note: By proclamation in 1962; July 4 became Philippine–American Friendship Day.
